analysis.investment_thesis: Ravelcare hits the SMILE sweet spot on size (100 Cr mcap) and promoter skin-in-the-game (72.94%), operating in India's huge digital BPC TAM. However, a 0.67% ROE at 19.2x P/E signals the business has not yet proven unit economics, making this a "watch, don't buy" until profitability appears.
key_strengths: Tiny 100 Cr mcap — classic small-cap sweet spot with info asymmetry
Strong promoter holding at 72.94% — high conviction skin-in-the-game
Digital-first BPC in a >50,000 Cr TAM with massive headroom
key_risks: ROE of 0.67% is abysmal — capital is not earning
P/E 19.2x is rich for a company with negligible profitability
Young company (2018) in hyper-competitive D2C beauty space (Nykaa, Mamaearth, Sugar)
red_flags: Revenue-profit gap: growing topline but earnings not scaling through
P/E >15x combined with sub-1% ROE suggests price is running ahead of fundamentals
analysis.detailed_analysis: From the SMILE lens, Ravelcare ticks three boxes cleanly: Small in size (100 Cr mcap — exactly where I hunt), promoter ownership of 72.94% (large aspiration, skin in game), and Extra-large market potential (Indian BPC is a secular consumption-upgrade story with digital penetration still under 20%). The company is at a potential inflection point — digital-first BPC brands are riding urbanization and formalization tailwinds.\n\nBut the arithmetic is uncomfortable: ROE at 0.67% means the business is barely generating returns on promoter capital, and paying 19.2x earnings for that is expensive. I want to see operating leverage kick in — gross margins expanding, marketing spend as % of sales declining, and ROE moving toward 15%+. Until then, this is a "track it quarterly" name, not a conviction buy. I'd revisit at a 25-30% lower price or after two quarters of visible margin expansion.
